text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Tallinn city council elected Ivi Eenmaa, director of the National Library, as new mayor.

- The justice ministry asked the security police to open a criminal case against two judges who presented forged certificates of proficiency in Estonian. Russian-speakers have to prove their knowledge of Estonian in order to keep certain state jobs.
- Interest paid on housing loans can be exempted from income tax retrospectively from January 1996, parliament decided.
- The opposition in Tallinn city council started a no-confidence motion against deputy mayor Kalev Kallo. The council will vote on the matter on May 15.
- Germany supports the admission of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania into Nato, German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said.
- The days of Estonian music are being held in Japan on May 10-20 with over 50 Estonian musicians performing.
- A majority at the parliament round-table meeting supported the idea of raising social tax and linking the sum of pensions to the amount that the person has paid in tax.
- A planned motorway between Tallinn and the southern town of Tartu ould need 155 million kroons next year, a project work-group decided.
